newsitem.title: NORWAY: Nordic financial sector abuzz with merger talk.
newsitem.headline: Nordic financial sector abuzz with merger talk.

text.p: The proposed merger of one of Norway's top banks and the country's largest insurance group may mark a new round of consolidation in the Nordic financial sector.
The sector is also becoming a battleground for banks and insurance companies looking for growth abroad, analysts said.
Norway's Storebrand ASA and Christiania Bank og Kreditkasse ASA said on Wednesday they planned to merge to form the sixth largest Nordic financial group.

The new company, Christiania, may be looking to expand in the Nordic financial sector, which also embraces Sweden, Finland, and Denmark, as well as growing further in the crowded home market, company executives said.

"There is still more to come," said Nils Ringdal at Dresdner Kleinwort Benson in London, asked if consolidation in the Norwegian financial sector would continue. "Certainly this is not the end of it either within Norway or across borders."

The merger plans between Christiania and Storebrand, which will be carried out by the end of the year, depending on government approval, coincided with a takeover battle between two other Norwegian banks.
Norway's top bank Den norske Bank (DnB) and Fokus Bank are bidding for Bolig og Naeringsbanken, a mortgage lender. DnB last year took over Vital Forsikring, Norway's second largest life insurer.
The latest big move in the Finnish financial sector was in 1995, when Unitas and Kansallis-Osake-Pankki (KOP) merged to form Merita Bank.
Talk of further consolidation has recently resumed in Helsinki, fuelled by activity elsewhere in the region; and a cocktail of rumours has helped drive gains in financial sector stocks.

One scenario is the possible consolidation of state-owned Postipankki with regional state financiers, and cooperative banking group OKOBank has said it would be interested in Postipankki if it came onto the market.

There has also been talk of more Swedish involvement as big Swedish banks Handelsbanken and S-E Banken intensify their business on Finnish soil -- insurer Skandia already has links with insurer Pohjola.
In February, Handelsbanken finalised its acquisition of mortgage lender Stadshypotek and Swedbank and Foreningsbanken announced they would merge.
Market players are convinced Sweden's Nordbanken and S-E-Banken will resume merger talks after previous talks ended without conclusion earlier this year.

Analysts say major Danish banks are not seen as likely to merge in the foreseeable future, having undergone a wave of consolidation already. The last took effect in January 1996, when the post office Girobank merged with savings bank Bikuben to create BG Bank, the country's third largest.
In Copenhagen, analysts generally expect any future mergers to be between small and medium-sized banks or for them to be swallowed by the big houses.
Another trend appears to be expansion elsewhere in the Nordic region. Danish market leader Den Danske Bank took a controlling interest in Sweden's Ostgota Enskilda Bank last month.
Unidanmark has denied market rumours of merger talks with Sweden's Nordbanken or S-E-Banken but sees Nordic expansion as a main strategic factor.
Aage Korsvold, chief executive officer at Storebrand, said the joint Christiania company may intensify its efforts in the other Nordic countries.
"The most important competitors in our home market are our Nordic competitors," he said. "Competition is strong and getting stronger."
Norway's central bank in an analysis this week said Norwegian financial institutions were small on a Nordic scale.

"Major structural changes can be expected in the banking sector in the next decade," the central bank said. "New institutions may emerge, and today's institutions will probably grow bigger and fewer."
